4.A. History and Development of the Company
Australian Oilseeds is an exempted company incorporated in the Cayman Islands on December 29, 2022.
On March 21, 2024, the Company consummated the previously announced business combination (the “Business Combination”) under the business combination agreement among the Company, EDOC Acquisition Corp. (“EDOC”), AOI, AOI Merger Sub Inc. (“Merger Sub”), and certain shareholders of AOI (the “AOI Sellers”), pursuant to which (a) Merger Sub merged with and into EDOC, with EDOC as the surviving entity and a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company, and with holders of EDOC securities receiving substantially identical securities of the Company, and (b) the Company acquired all of the issued and outstanding ordinary shares of AOI from the AOI Sellers in exchange for ordinary shares of the Company, with AOI becoming a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company.
As of the date of this Annual Report, the Company’s operating subsidiaries are RentBuddyUK; Magic Mission International Limited (“Magic Mission”), a wholly owned British Virgin Islands subsidiary through which the Company conducts its TenantGraph platform; and Vellexa Group Inc. (“Vellexa”), a wholly owned Wyoming corporation that carries on corporate administration and strategic holding activities.
The Company’s principal executive offices are located at 126 – 142 Cowcumbla Street, Cootamundra, Site 2: 52 Fuller Drive Cootamundra, PO Box 263 Cootamundra, Australia 2590, and its telephone number is +02 6942 4347. The Company’s registered office is located at Kensington House, 69 Dr. Roy’s Drive, P.O. Box 2510, George Town, Grand Cayman KY1-1104, Cayman Islands. The Company’s website is https://www.oilseeds.com.au/. The SEC maintains a website at http://www.sec.gov that contains reports and other information that we file with or furnish electronically with the SEC.
Material Developments During Fiscal Year 2026
Conversion of Convertible Debt. On July 10, 2025, the Company received a conversion notice from Arena Investors LP (“Arena”) for conversion of USD 250,000 of convertible debt, which the Company has duly executed and issued 420,066 Class A ordinary shares as per instruction from Arena.
Settlement with Arena. On December 22, 2025, the Company entered into a Confidential Settlement and Release Agreement (the “Arena Settlement Agreement”) with the holders of the 10% Original Issue Discount Secured Convertible Debenture due September 21, 2025 issued to Arena (the “Arena Holders”) to settle all outstanding disputes relating to the securities purchase agreement dated August 23, 2023 among the Company, AOI, EDOC, certain subsidiaries of AOI and Arena, and the related documents. Under the Arena Settlement Agreement, the Company agreed to pay US$112,500 to Arena Limited SPV, LLC for the benefit of the Arena Holders. The Arena Settlement Agreement provides that, upon the Arena Holders’ receipt in full of that amount, the securities purchase agreement, the debenture, the Deed of Guarantee and Indemnity, the General Security Deed, the Mortgage Term Deed, the Intercompany Loan Agreement, the Payment Directions Deed, the Subordination Deeds and the other related agreements terminate, and that within three business days after receipt the Arena Holders will release the related security interests, including registrations on the Australian Personal Property Securities Register. The Arena Holders agreed to release the Company and all guarantors, including Mr. Gary Seaton, from claims relating to those agreements, other than indemnification claims under Section 5.10 of the securities purchase agreement, and the Company agreed to release the Arena Holders. Separately, on December 11, 2025, the Company entered into a Confidential Settlement and Release Agreement (the “ELOC Settlement Agreement”) to settle all outstanding disputes relating to the Purchase Agreement dated as of March 5, 2024 between the Company and the ELOC Investor, under which the Company had the right to sell up to US$50 million of Ordinary Shares to the ELOC Investor (the “ELOC”). Under the ELOC Settlement Agreement, in full and final satisfaction of all of the Company’s obligations under the Purchase Agreement, including its obligations to issue and register commitment fee shares, the Company agreed to issue 1,750,000 Ordinary Shares to the ELOC Investor.
Acquisition of RentBuddyUK Limited. On April 24, 2026, the Company entered into a share purchase agreement (the “Share Purchase Agreement”) with Hailing Fan (the “Seller”), pursuant to which the Company agreed to acquire a 51% interest in RentBuddyUK. RentBuddyUK is a company that specializes in rent guarantee services designed to provide landlords with stable and predictable rental income. On June 29, 2026, the Company entered into an Amendment to Share Purchase Agreement (the “Amendment”) with the Seller and RentBuddyUK. The Amendment revised the legal structure by which the Company acquired its 51% interest in RentBuddyUK. Instead of the Company purchasing 5,100 existing ordinary shares of RentBuddyUK from the Seller, RentBuddyUK allotted and issued 10,409 newly issued ordinary shares of RentBuddyUK to the Company, and the Seller retained the 10,000 ordinary shares of RentBuddyUK held by it. Immediately following such allotment and issuance, the issued share capital of RentBuddyUK consisted of 20,409 ordinary shares, of which the Company held 10,409 ordinary shares, representing approximately 51% of the issued share capital of RentBuddyUK, and the Seller held 10,000 ordinary shares. The allotment was reported to the Registrar of Companies of the United Kingdom (Companies House) by a return of allotment filed on June 18, 2026, which states an allotment date of April 26, 2026, and the allotment and issuance were ratified and confirmed pursuant to the Amendment. The total purchase price for the Company’s 51% interest in RentBuddyUK remained US$5,326,840, and the economic terms of the transaction were otherwise unchanged. On June 29, 2026, the Company closed the transaction. By the closing, US$3,672,000 was paid by the Company to the account designated in accordance with the Share Purchase Agreement, as amended by the Amendment. Of the total purchase price of US$5,326,840, US$918,000 was previously paid upon execution of the Share Purchase Agreement, and the remaining US$736,840 is payable to RentBuddyUK, as subscription monies for the 10,409 ordinary shares, within six months following the closing in accordance with the Share Purchase Agreement, as amended by the Amendment. As RentBuddyUK is a subsidiary of the Company, this amount is an intra-group payable that is eliminated on consolidation. Although the 10,409 ordinary shares were issued to the Company by RentBuddyUK, the US$918,000 and US$3,672,000 payments were made to the Seller rather than to RentBuddyUK, and RentBuddyUK has recorded the amounts so paid as a loan receivable from the Seller, which amounted to AUD$6,529,191 as of June 30, 2026, was interest-free and unsecured and was repayable on or before October 2, 2026. The loan was repaid in full in USDT. See “Item 7.B. Related Party Transactions.” (See Forms 6-K furnished April 30, 2026 and July 2, 2026.)
Equity Financings. During the fiscal year, the Company completed two private placements of units consisting of ordinary shares and warrants: (i) a placement of 2,000,000 units at US$1.00 per unit for gross proceeds of US$2.0 million, which closed on March 6, 2026; and (ii) a placement of 16,800,000 units at US$0.50 per unit for gross proceeds of US$8.4 million, which closed on April 17, 2026. Each unit consisted of one ordinary share and one warrant to purchase up to two ordinary shares. See “Item 10.C. Material Contracts.” See “Item 5. Operating and Financial Review and Prospects — Liquidity and Capital Resources” for further discussion.
Changes in Directors and Management. On October 23, 2025, Mr. Kapil Singh resigned from his position with the Company as a director. On October 24, 2025, each of Mr. Kevin Chen and Mr. Phaneesh Murthy resigned from his position with the Company as a director. Effective on November 5, 2025, the Board appointed each of Mr. Long (Leo) Yi and Ms. Elena Cozneac as a new independent director and Mr. Jamie Mohammed Zamal as a new executive director to fill the existing vacancies on the Board, and appointed Mr. Zamal to serve as Co-Chief Executive Officer of the Company, alongside Mr. Gary Seaton, who continued in his role as Co-Chief Executive Officer. On January 8, 2026, Mr. Gowri Shankar tendered his resignation from his position as a member of the Board and any and all committees, effective on January 9, 2026. Effective on January 9, 2026, Mr. Ho Yeung Lee was appointed as a director of the Board.
